findings.summary: The Vercel AI Gateway account ran out of funds (HTTP 402 insufficient_funds) after the 3rd of 15 pre-committed compilation attempts, blocking 12/15 compilations and starving verification of any further real candidates. Re-confirmed live by a fresh probe after the run.
findings.requiredAction: A human must top up the Vercel AI Gateway account balance. No production code change is implicated or warranted.

findings.summary: Under a genuine, live infrastructure funding failure hitting mid-verification, the system never produced a false VERIFIED result - every affected candidate correctly surfaced as FAILED. This mirrors the same safe-failure discipline this engagement has repeatedly certified in prior phases (e.g. OPEN-4's condition-suspicion classifier), now observed under a real, unscripted fault rather than a synthetic test.

The deterministic Layer 1 reconciliation engine caught a real compiled-IR hallucination on this genuinely novel package (a fabricated $100,000,000 AMOUNT value with no matching source-side figure) without needing any AI call, correctly forcing that candidate to a non-VERIFIED state.

findings.classification: EVALUATION_DEFECT (of this validation run, not of Headroom)
findings.summary: The pre-committed 15-candidate compile cap, combined with the account running dry after only 3 real compiles, means this run cannot answer its own core mission question (whether the compiler generalizes to a genuinely novel LTV/margin-call-based covenant style) at any meaningful statistical confidence. The two independent ground-truth reviewers (184 combined claims, strong qualitative convergence including catching the same non-obvious amendment-effect) represent substantial completed, reusable work that is currently unscored against Headroom's output.
findings.requiredAction: Resume compilation/verification/coverage from where this run left off once the Gateway account is funded, then complete the claim-level comparison against the already-built ground truth.
